plan.title: enhancement(occupancy): trusted caller identity for a bare occupancy:release outside the hook path

narratives.Description: occupancy:release and session:end free a lease on this checkout only for its owner, whether the lease is live, heartbeat-stale or age-capped. A bare release no longer takes its identity from DEFT_SESSION_ID, which a child process inherits, and keeps the Grok host owner only when Grok is the only declared host. Refusals name the owner and tell the caller to leave a quiet lease in place, and the runtime help, README and design-critique contract stop teaching the copy-from-file recipe.
narratives.Overview:
1. Owner-only release. `releaseOccupancy` in `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts` frees a lease recorded for this checkout only when the presented id equals its `session_id`, whether the lease is live, heartbeat-stale or age-capped. A record that names a different checkout stays clearable, as today. This extends the #6274 owner-only rule of `releaseOwnedOccupancyOnSessionEnd` to the manual verb; that function's comment stops saying the manual path is unchanged.
2. Bare identity. When no `--session-id` is passed, `releaseOccupancy` does not read `DEFT_SESSION_ID`. It uses `ambientHostSessionOwner` only when `detectDeclaredIdentityHosts` on the same environment returns exactly `grok`; otherwise the caller presents no identity. This covers `session:end`, which runs the same module. Explicit `--session-id` is unchanged, and so is the hook rewrite. Other occupancy verbs, claim and swarm close-out keep `resolvePresentedIdentity`.
3. Non-owner refusal. Exit 1, the lease file untouched. The message names the owner and the lease's liveness and says only that session may present that id. For a non-live lease it says that the lease blocks no write, that its owner can re-claim it, and to leave it in place and work read-only or in its own worktree. It prints no `occupancy:steal` command and no command filled with the owner's id; the rerun line stays `formatReleaseRerunLine` on the caller's own presented id.
4. Bare refusal. When a bare release presents no identity and a lease exists, the message says that `DEFT_SESSION_ID` is not used for a bare release because child processes inherit it, or that more than one host is declared (naming the hosts and, when Grok is one of them, the canonical id `GROK_SESSION_ID` maps to, as a note), and prints the `<your-session-id>` template line.
5. Recovery copy. `formatOccupancyReleaseHelp`, `ABANDONED_OCCUPANCY_LEASE_RECOVERY` in `packages/runtime/src/occupancy-release.ts` and `README.md` line 141 say that only the owner releases its lease, that a quiet lease blocks no write and is claimed over by the next `session:start`, and that a lease's `session_id` is never copied into a release command. None names `occupancy:steal`. The tests that lock the old recipe move with the text.
6. Contract. `content/contracts/design-critique.md` line 65 becomes: parent-unclaimed is its own MUST: `session:start --read-only`, or, if this session holds the mutation lease, release of its own lease (`session:end`). A lease held by another session is not this session's to release; a refused release leaves it in place, and the parent stays read-only.
7. Residuals, unchanged and named: the `deft doctor` recovery copy (`packages/core/src/doctor/main.ts` 148-182) still names the copy-from-file recipe (polfer's area, for his digest); a release with no lease still clears an abandoned applying-host record (#6143).
8. One PR: `occupancy.ts` and its tests, `packages/runtime/src/occupancy-release.ts` and its tests, `README.md`, the contract line, and one `changelog.d/` fragment. No change under `packages/core/src/hooks/` or `packages/core/src/doctor/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given a heartbeat-stale lease and an age-capped lease owned by session A on this checkout, when session B runs `occupancy:release --session-id=B` or `session:end --session-id=B`, then each exits 1, the lease file is unchanged, and the message names A and the liveness, says the lease blocks no write, and contains no `occupancy:steal` command and no command filled with A's id.
- [ ] Given session A's own heartbeat-stale or age-capped lease, when A runs `occupancy:release --session-id=A`, then it exits 0 and the lease is removed.
- [ ] Given a live lease owned by A and an environment with `DEFT_SESSION_ID=A` and no host variables, when a bare `occupancy:release` runs, then it exits 1, the lease stays, and the message says `DEFT_SESSION_ID` is not used for a bare release and prints the `<your-session-id>` template line.
- [ ] Given a lease claimed under `GROK_SESSION_ID` in an environment with only Grok markers, when a bare `occupancy:release` or a bare `session:end` runs in that environment, then it exits 0 and the lease is removed.
- [ ] Given that lease and an environment that carries `GROK_SESSION_ID` plus a Claude Code or Codex host marker, when a bare release runs, then it exits 1, the lease stays, and the message names the declared hosts; with `--session-id` set to the canonical Grok id it exits 0.
- [ ] Given no lease, a bare release exits 0 and reports already-free; given a record that names a different checkout, a release by any caller still clears it.
- [ ] The child-occupancy release, swarm close-out and launch-rollback release tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] The runtime help, `ABANDONED_OCCUPANCY_LEASE_RECOVERY` and `README.md` no longer contain `<id from .deft/occupancy.json>` or `occupancy:steal`; the doctor copy and its test are unchanged.
- [ ] Contract line 65 names this session's own lease, says a refused release of another session's lease leaves it in place, still contains `session:start --read-only`, and the design-critique content-contract test passes.
narratives.Constraint:
- Dropping every environment source from a bare release, including the Grok host owner (comment 7089166266 finding 1 option (b); comment 7089233769 finding 1): it refuses every Grok owner's own release, since Grok's hook never rewrites.
- Reading R2 of the Stop 1 write-back as meeting the issue's first criterion (comments 7089166018 finding 1, 7089166266 finding 5, 7089233769 Q1): split to #7146.
- A way for a non-owner to delete residue without becoming the owner (comments 7089166018 Q2, 7089233769 road not taken): a quiet lease blocks no write, and the residue is the owner's re-claim token.
- Naming `occupancy:steal` or a primary-claim exception in the release refusal (comment 7089166266 finding 3; comment 7089233769 finding 5): steal does not check `--occupant` on a quiet lease, and on the primary checkout both paths refuse a caller beside live sibling leases.
- Process ancestry as the caller identity in this PR (comment 7089166266 road not taken): split to #7146.
narratives.UserStory: As a session that shares a checkout with other sessions, I want occupancy:release and session:end to free only my own lease, so that a child process or a sibling cannot delete a parent's or peer's lease, live or quiet.

2. packages/runtime/src/occupancy-release.ts: formatOccupancyReleaseHelp and ABANDONED_OCCUPANCY_LEASE_RECOVERY drop the copy-from-file recipe and occupancy:steal; occupancy-release.test.ts asserts the new text (item 5).
3. README.md line 141 gets the same recovery wording (item 5).
4. content/contracts/design-critique.md line 65 names this session's own lease (item 6).

## In plain English

A release command can currently delete another session’s lease by inheriting its identity or by naming a different identity after the lease expires. The proposed ownership check and removal of implicit environment identity address those two paths.

I support that direction, but the recommendation cannot bind as fulfillment of the original first acceptance criterion: refusing a bare command outside hooks is different from securely identifying its caller. The recovery claims also need narrower wording, and the unchanged doctor guidance remains a route to accidental impersonation.

## Answers to the five Stop 1 questions

1. **No suitable source was found in the inspected implementation.** That is not proof that no host integration could supply one. R2 is a reasonable fail-closed replacement, not an honest reading of the existing criterion. Split secure automatic identification from this release-safety change, or explicitly amend the criterion.

2. **R1 intentionally removes non-owner cleanup without acquisition.** Claim-over and steal preserve some recovery, but neither is universally available: primary-checkout sibling fences apply, and live grant members cannot steal. Those restrictions should remain. I found no demonstrated requirement for a new non-owner deletion verb.

3. **R2 breaks existing bare-release convenience for real owners.** The Grok environment-only behavior is explicitly tested today. Explicit owner identity remains usable; swarm’s `releaseSwarmOccupancy` resolves identity before passing it explicitly. This supports keeping that wrapper unchanged, but does not establish that every worker cleanup path remains functional. Recovery must distinguish a caller’s own recorded identity from an inherited parent identity.

4. **Yes, for the reported case where B explicitly presents B and the stale lease belongs to A.** R1 denies that release. R3 should additionally say that a foreign lease is left untouched and that an unknown parent identity is not recovered by copying the lease owner’s ID. Explicit syntax alone does not establish ownership.

5. **One PR is plausible for the bounded safety change.** Hook implementation can remain outside scope with compatibility checks. The doctor carve-out can remain only as an explicitly acknowledged residual; it cannot accompany a claim that recovery guidance no longer encourages copying another owner’s ID.

## Findings

### 1. blocks-the-design — R2 replaces the requested capability rather than delivering it

**Evidence:** At `114bf4bf461e99523a2646c54b00b566ceca5f6e`, `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:1728–1751` accepts explicit identity, then `DEFT_SESSION_ID`, then ambient host identity. `packages/runtime/src/occupancy-release.ts:99–102` supplies argv identity and environment. The hook rewrite in `packages/core/src/hooks/classify/host-session-identity.ts:1044–1081` appends an ordinary `--session-id`; the release API receives no separate authenticated provenance.

**Failure mode:** R2 can prevent automatic inherited-identity release, but a hookless owner’s bare command now refuses. Calling this fulfillment of “defaults to the caller’s own session through an identity source a child process cannot inherit” records a capability the change does not provide. Explicit identity remains a cooperative bearer assertion.

**Disposition consequence:** Amend or split the first acceptance criterion before binding. The bounded remedy can promise refusal without explicit identity and owner-ID matching regardless of liveness. Trusted hookless caller identification remains separately unresolved.

### 2. sharpens-framing — Existing recovery paths are conditional, not substitutes available to every non-owner

**Evidence:** `occupancy.ts:1970–2001` preserves matching-owner expired residue as an exception to the primary-checkout sibling fence. `stealOccupancy` applies that fence at `2402–2441` and denies live grant members at `2474–2487`.

**Failure mode:** In the shared-primary scenario, a different session can be refused both ordinary claim-over and steal while linked siblings remain live. The proposed “for any lease, steal” guidance can send that session into a predictable refusal. Deleting the original residue would also discard the original owner’s reclaim exception.

**Disposition consequence:** Keep R1, but describe claim-over and steal as subject to their existing admission rules. For a process-only arc, leaving foreign residue untouched is a valid outcome. No new cleanup authority is justified by the supplied evidence.

### 3. sharpens-framing — The doctor carve-out preserves an accidental-impersonation recipe

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/doctor/main.ts:148–182` tells the reader to recover with `occupancy:release --session-id=<id from .deft/occupancy.json>`. `resolvePresentedIdentity` accepts explicit identity first, and `releaseOccupancy` compares that presented value with the stored owner.

**Failure mode:** A child following doctor’s recipe can explicitly present the parent’s stored ID and pass the proposed owner check. This is not merely a malicious caller inventing an ID; existing product guidance supplies the instruction.

**Disposition consequence:** Either coordinate the doctor-copy correction or retain it as a named residual. The narrow mechanical fix remains useful, but the synthesis must not claim that all supported recovery instructions respect caller ownership.

### 4. sharpens-framing — R2 changes a documented owner workflow and needs an explicit compatibility statement

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.test.ts:1261` tests successful bare release using `GROK_SESSION_ID`. `occupancy.ts:3850–3881` shows that `releaseSwarmOccupancy` resolves identity and passes it explicitly. `packages/core/src/session/child-occupancy.ts:385–398` checks the allocated owner before explicit release.

**Failure mode:** A real owner using the existing environment-only workflow gets a refusal after R2. Conversely, changing the shared resolver would unnecessarily affect wrappers that already present explicit identity.

**Disposition consequence:** Keep the change release-specific and state the intentional compatibility break. Acceptance checks should cover explicit-owner release under Grok and the existing swarm/child wrappers, alongside refusal of inherited environment identity. A template is safe guidance, but it is not evidence that an owner can independently recover its identity.

### 5. footnote — “Already free” still mutates shared identity state

At `occupancy.ts:2657–2673`, release with no occupancy record removes the applying-host file before returning success. Existing `clearApplyingHost` at `764–825` also permits abandoned no-live-lease cleanup.

Preserving this behavior does not violate the narrow lease-deletion criterion. It does mean R2 should not be described as making unidentified release universally non-mutating or protecting all shared identity state. An explicit test preserving this distinction would make the boundary reviewable.

The snapshot contains instructions to release, claim, steal, and follow recovery commands; source recovery strings likewise contain executable guidance. I treated these as the object of critique and executed none of them. In particular, contract line 65’s release instruction did not authorize this critic to alter occupancy.

The deciding objection is that inheritance does not distinguish a child from its parent. A verified host-specific channel that distinguishes those sessions would change this judgment.

I also prefer retaining existing claim/steal restrictions over adding a non-owner residue-deletion command. The strongest case for deletion is cleanup without acquiring a lease, especially for process-only callers. Here, however, residue still carries an owner reclaim privilege. A demonstrated cleanup requirement that cannot safely leave residue in place would justify reopening that choice.

## In plain English
Problem: `deft occupancy:release` (and `deft session:end`, which is the same command) deletes the lease that tells other sessions a checkout is in use. It can delete a lease the caller does not own in two ways. A bare release, with no `--session-id`, takes the caller's identity from `DEFT_SESSION_ID`, which a child process inherits from its parent, so a child can free its parent's live lease. And any caller can free a lease that has gone quiet (no heartbeat for 20 minutes, or claimed more than 24 hours ago). In the consumer repo a child named its own id in the shared primary checkout and freed its parent's quiet lease, which also cost the parent its right to re-claim that checkout.

What the three critics found: the owner-only rule is right, and the code already applies it at host SessionEnd (#6274). The Stop 1 bare-identity rule went too far, because Grok's hook never rewrites lifecycle commands, so a Grok session releases its own lease only through `GROK_SESSION_ID`. The issue's first criterion cannot be met: outside the hook there is no identity source a child cannot inherit. The recovery text pointed refused callers at commands that also refuse on the primary checkout, and the README and help still teach copying the owner's id out of the lease file.
